senses.gloss:
Puñji-ṣṭha is found in the Yajurveda Saṃhitās^1 and later,^2
apparently meaning ‘fisherman,’ though Mahīdhara^3 explains
it as ‘bird-catcher.’ Cf. Pauñjiṣṭha.
1) Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xvi. 27; Tait-
tirīya Saṃhitā, iv. 5, 4, 2; Maitrāyaṇī
Saṃhitā, ii. 9, 5; Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā,
xvii. 13.
2) Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, x. 7;
Pāṇini, viii. 3, 97.
3) On Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xvi. 27.

Puñjīla is found in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā^1 and the Taittirīya
Brāhmaṇa^2 in the sense of a ‘bundle’ of grass, being a variant
of Piñjūla.
1) vi. 1, 1, 7; 2, 4, 3.
2) i. 7, 6, 4; ii. 7, 9, 5.
